findings.description: Long-lived AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the Lambda function's environment variables and committed to source control. Anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration or repository access can retrieve them and impersonate the associated IAM principal.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so environment variables (which here contain secrets) are protected only by the default AWS-managed key and are readable by any principal allowed to describe the function. A customer-managed CMK with restricted key policy would enforce a separate authorization boundary.

The function uses nodejs12.x, a runtime that has reached end of life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving known vulnerabilities in the runtime and its bundled OpenSSL/libc dependencies unpatched.

No vpc_config block is defined, so the function runs outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or NACL boundary, enabling unmonitored data egress if the function or its dependencies are compromised.
